bull.t: Strong product demand and revenue growth
bull.b: Multiple products are producing strong prescription, account, and unit growth, reducing reliance on a single franchise. Broad demand across dry eye, surgical, and retina offerings supports continued revenue expansion and provides a stronger base for commercial leverage over the next several quarters.

bull.t: High-margin products and improving cash generation
bull.b: Very high gross margins and a turnaround to positive operating and free cash flow indicate improving underlying economics despite reported losses. If sustained, stronger cash conversion can fund commercialization, support liquidity, and eventually help the company reduce reliance on external capital.

bull.t: Portfolio expansion strengthens ophthalmic market position
bull.b: Adding TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry-eye offerings with a drop-free treatment that complements VEVYE and can give physicians more prescribing options. The expanded portfolio and salesforce may deepen customer relationships, improve commercial productivity, and support durable category positioning.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: A debt-funded balance sheet with limited equity protection reduces financial flexibility if operating results weaken. Higher leverage can constrain investment, increase refinancing exposure, and make acquisition or commercialization spending more dependent on sustained cash generation.

bear.t: Persistent losses despite strong gross margins
bear.b: Strong product economics have not yet translated into dependable profitability, indicating that operating costs or other headwinds remain substantial. Continued losses could limit internally funded growth, weaken balance-sheet resilience, and make earnings quality less consistent over the next several quarters.

bear.t: Execution and reimbursement risks could delay growth
bear.b: Meeting annual guidance depends on a large second-half acceleration across product launches, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and acquisition integration. Reimbursement pressure in ASC settings adds another structural hurdle that could slow adoption and make revenue timing less predictable.
